qualitativeDistinctness: Actual health and population study anchors the programme; institutional and organisational analysis is complementary. The label avoids claiming a specialist healthcare-policy or healthcare-management degree.

The programmes share 18 courses, with 6 different courses (45 EC) in each. The closest adds biological/disease science, accounting, microeconomics and econometrics; the related programme adds social and abnormal psychology, youth resilience, assessment/psychotherapy concepts, modern sociology and constitutional comparison. Their organising questions differ between population/institutional analysis and development, mental health and social conditions across the lifecourse.

Fivecourses/37.5EC differ fromtheclosest andeightcourses/60ECfromthelifecourseoption. Startup/prototyping,customerinsights,marketresearch anddigitalstrategy shiftwork towardinnovationdevelopment andadoption. Thehealth-needs core remains,so thedifference isnotgenericbusiness withouthealthsubstance.
